body: Thanks for reporting this, I'll have a look
@codeskyblue  It seems OK here... maybe it was some instability in Github API... can you re-run the job and check if it works, please?

I'm running into the same issue. A restart worked once for me, but a second time it did not. Would of course rather not be restarting my jobs if I don't have to, either.

Might be worth adding a little debug output showing what, if anything, is returned from the Github API for this initial call yielding `Unable to get goreleaser version`.

```shell
0.38s$ curl -sL https://git.io/goreleaser | bash
Unable to get goreleaser version.
```

> https://travis-ci.org/whilei/janus/builds/252094592?utm_source=github_status&utm_medium=notification

do you have a `GITHUB_TOKEN` set for your build?

if not, it is accessing the API without a token, which has a very small rate limit. And you are sharing it with several travis users... so the failure is probably because of that.

We are working on solving this by generating the script on every release with the version hard coded, so we don't need to get the latest version for it to work. This may take some time to be implemented.

The quick win is to put the token on your travis-ci.

If it still not working, your token probably hit rate limit as well...

issue.title: Improve get script to not use the API

milestone.title: v1.0.0
milestone.description: Intended to be the first stable solution, with most of the features implemented.

issue.body:
To get the latest version, we may use a simple curl command like this instead:

```
$ curl -sL -o /dev/null -w %{url_effective} https://github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/releases/latest | rev | cut -f1 -d'/'| rev
v0.26.1
```

No API access means no problems with rate limiting, solving intermittent errors like #157

We may do the same in godownloader. cc @client9
